pr_body:
### Summary

`rails dbconsole` should default to `include_password`

rails dbconsole will inject the password into the DB console if one is configured and the `include_password` flag is enabled.  Let’s enable this flag by default.

For years, developers have been running `rails dbconsole` in staging or production and pasting in a password, not even knowing that `rails dbconsole -p` would do what they actually wanted and apply the credentials already configured in their `config/database.yml`.  Let's apply the principle of least surprise and change the default behavior to what most folks would expect and improve the user experience.

### Other Information

* fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/45901
pr_comments:
Thank you for the pull request. The reason why this isn't default is that the password goes to the history logging of commands, and on the PID of the process which will very much cause security problems.

See https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0abf0da0016abc455145810d7060a10e0b56b0b6

Both `mysql` and `psql` support providing password through an options file. It is more correct to avoid the security concerns that way, instead of leaving responsibility to clueless humans to obtain and supply password to the remote host securely.

@akostadinov I'm not sure but a quick google search says at least for postgresql to use the `--passfile` flag for that, is that what you mean? [[ref](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-connect.html#LIBPQ-CONNECT-PASSFILE)]
@zzak , I didn't find this option but it should do the job. For MySQL I think there is no such flag. But one can use a custom options file (`my.cnf`).

issue_context.title: bin/rails dbconsole should include_password by default
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a Rails `config/database.yml` with a `password` required to connect
2. Run `rails dbconsole`
3. See prompt for database password, despite password being configured/available
4. Run `rails dbconsole -p`
5. See dbconsole properly load and use credentials to connect to database for DB console session

### Expected behavior
Whenever a Rails app has credentials like a password configured for a database, the database console session should use those credentials vs. prompting the user to re-enter a password interactively.  When credentials are not configured and a password is required, we should prompt then.

This behavior is implemented since early Rails versions but is disabled by default.  I propose we enable the proper password behavior by default.

### Actual behavior
`bin/rails dbconsole` always prompts for a password, even when one is configured for the app.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: All (6.x, 7.x, head)

**Ruby version**: All

review_comments:
If we're setting the default value of a boolean param to true, would it even be possible for it to ever be false? Seems like the param should be deprecated/removed if it isn't going to have an effect any more.

This will also definitely need a changelog entry

Thanks for looking at this PR! I really appreciate it.

The dbconsole command documents flags to both enable/disable this option:

```
Usage:
  rails dbconsole [options]

Options:
  -e, [--environment=ENVIRONMENT]                    # Specifies the environment to run this dbconsole under (test/development/production).
  -p, [--include-password], [--no-include-password]  # Automatically provide the password from database.yml
                                                     # Default: true
      [--mode=MODE]                                  # Automatically put the sqlite3 database in the specified mode (html, list, line, column).
                                                     # Possible values: html, list, line, column
      [--header], [--no-header]
  --db, [--database=DATABASE]                        # Specifies the database to use.
  ```

I believe boolean options provide a command line flag to both enable or disable the value.  Currently, this option is disabled, but running `bin/rails dbconsole --include-password` will enable it.

With this PR changing the default value to true, it can still be disabled if users specify the `bin/rails dbconsole --no-include-password` flag on the command.  I've just confirmed this flag will still disable the value even with a default of true.
I've added a `railties` CHANGELOG entry in b98e8918749b424f95552dbb6f11a6d481609636 describing this behavior change.
